source_tier: trade-technical (Oil & Gas Journal) + operator technical paper (ConocoPhillips)
source_notes: The historic (now mothballed) Kenai export train's liquefaction compressors were shaft-driven by on-site single-shaft Frame 5 gas turbines from 1969 startup - mechanical drive, confirmed independently by Oil & Gas Journal and by ConocoPhillips's own liquefaction-technology paper (the plant's original designer/operator). The current proposed import-conversion design (Trans-Foreland Cool Down) does not reactivate these turbines; it adds a 1,000-hp electric BOG booster compressor and electric/submerged-combustion vaporizers, far below the 50 MW threshold. MECHANICAL-DRIVE DETAIL: Original 1969 liquefaction plant used single-shaft GE Frame 5 gas turbines to directly (mechanically) drive the LNG refrigeration compressors - shaft power only, no generator. Two independent verified sources confirm 'Frame 5' direct-drive turbines at Kenai; neither yields a verifiable aggregate MW/bhp figure (a candidate 84,600 bhp / 63.1 MW figure FAILED independent verification and was dropped). ORCHESTRATOR NOTE: Historic mothballed export train only; MW never publicly quantified, so no figure is asserted. The 'Import Terminal' unit-row is a separate proposed facility at the same site but CaptiveGasPower is a project-level field, so the value is staged to every unit-row per project-level propagation.

source_tier: operator site + BC EAO GHG Technical Data Report + GE press release + provincial air permit
source_notes: LNG Canada's own site states it uses aero-derivative gas turbines to drive refrigeration compressors, with a 'cogeneration' feature using turbine exhaust waste heat instead of a gas-fired boiler, plus BC Hydro for ~20% of total power demand. The mechanical-drive configuration, turbine count (2/train) and model (GE LMS100) are independently confirmed by (a) the EPC joint-venture's BC Energy Regulator waste-discharge authorization air-emissions permit booklet, which states each train's two refrigerant-compressor systems 'are driven by gas powered turbines' whose exhaust feeds waste-heat-recovery units 'for process heating needs' (i.e. NOT power generation), and (b) LNG Canada's own BC EAO GHG Management Technical Data Report naming GE LMS100 and the 93.4 MW rating. GE's own project announcement corroborates model/rating. MECHANICAL-DRIVE DETAIL: 4x GE LMS100(-PB) aeroderivative gas turbines (2 per train, 2 trains in Phase 1), each ~105 MW simple-cycle at ISO per GE; LNG Canada's own BC EAO GHG Management Technical Data Report cites a tested output rating of 93.4 MW per unit as its emissions basis. Each turbine's free power turbine is coupled directly to a refrigerant compressor string - shaft power only, no generator. Aggregate Phase-1 mechanical shaft output ~374-420 MW; a 4-train build-out doubles to 8 turbines per the same filing. ORCHESTRATOR NOTE: RE-VERIFIED UNCHANGED (blue): GEM already carries True. No paste needed - included so the workbook records that the existing value was independently re-confirmed this batch.

source_tier: primary/regulatory (US DOE Environmental Assessment DOE/EA-2226) + operator + trade
source_notes: Each built Fast LNG unit is an entirely off-grid three-jackup installation: one platform (Pioneer III) carries three ~11 MW Siemens SGT-400 simple-cycle gas turbines generating all facility/utility electric power, per the DOE Environmental Assessment DOE/EA-2226 (primary regulatory) and New Fortress's own project page. A separate platform (Pioneer II) runs a Baker Hughes LM6000PF+ gas turbine mechanically driving the IPSMR refrigerant compressor. No shore/CFE electrical connection appears anywhere in the DOE docket or corporate materials. MECHANICAL-DRIVE DETAIL: 1x Baker Hughes LM6000PF+ gas-turbine-driven compressor per FLNG unit, mechanically driving the main IPSMR refrigerant compressor on the liquefaction platform (Pioneer II) - not a generator; shaft MW undisclosed in any verified source. ELECTRIC CAPACITY: 33 MW per built FLNG unit (3x ~11 MW Siemens SGT-400 simple-cycle); 66 MW across the two authorised units FLNG1+FLNG2.

source_tier: primary/regulatory (AGDC Resource Report 1, FERC Docket CP17-178)
source_notes: AGDC's Resource Report 1 for the Alaska LNG Project (FERC Docket CP17-178, hosted by Alaska DEC) describes a dedicated on-site power system for the Nikiski Liquefaction Facility and Marine Terminal: onsite power 'would be derived from multiple gas turbine generators in an "N"+1 configuration' (plus one in reserve), and 'During normal operations, the power generation facility would supply 124 megawatts (MW).' The same passage states 'The plant is not designed to export power to the grid' - i.e. off-grid, purpose-built captive generation, unambiguously above the >50 MW threshold. Separately (mechanical=True), the Gas Treatment Plant uses natural-gas turbine-driven compressors totalling approximately 298,000 ISO horsepower across six units - shaft power, excluded from the 124 MW electric figure. MECHANICAL-DRIVE DETAIL: Each of the 3 LNG trains has 2 refrigerant compression strings, each driven directly by a natural gas turbine (mechanical/shaft drive, no generator) - 6 turbines total, combined ~800,000 ISO horsepower for refrigeration compression. Separate from the 124 MW electric-generation plant; produces zero MWe. NOTE: the 800,000 ISO-hp figure could not be cleanly verified (see verification_log) and is reported as background, not as a cited claim. ELECTRIC CAPACITY: 124. ORCHESTRATOR NOTE: RE-VERIFIED UNCHANGED (blue): GEM already carries True. No paste needed. NOTE: one of the two originally-cited URLs (FERC FEIS Volume 1) was dropped at the QC gate - it does not contain the claim. AGDC's Resource Report 1 does, verbatim, including 'The plant is not designed to export power to the grid.'

source_tier: OEM press release (GE) + 2 independent trade outlets + EPC contractor project page
source_notes: Two distinct turbine populations on site: (1) GE Frame 7/MS7001/7EA gas turbines in direct mechanical-drive service on the liquefaction train's refrigeration compressors, and (2) three dedicated GE LM2500+ aeroderivative gas turbine-GENERATORS supplying the site's electric power. Confirmed by GE's own 2015 long-term-service-agreement release (vendor of record) and corroborated by two independent trade-press reports plus EPC contractor McDermott's project page ('four refrigeration compressors, two gas turbines'). No source indicates electric-motor compressors or bulk SEIN grid supply. MECHANICAL-DRIVE DETAIL: 2x GE Frame 7 / MS7001 ('7EA') gas turbines drive 4 centrifugal refrigeration compressors for the single-train ConocoPhillips Optimized Cascade process (propane/ethylene/methane loops). Shaft MW not disclosed in any available source (7EA units are generically ~85 MW-class, but no Peru-specific figure is published) - reported as turbine count/model only.

source_tier: primary/regulatory (US DOE order) + licensor (Air Products) + trade
source_notes: Phase 1 (under construction, single 3.25 Mtpa APCI C3MR train, first cargo shipped July 2026) is mechanically driven: gas turbines directly drive the MR and propane refrigerant compressors (shaft power, no generator). The environmental-authorization filing also lists an existing/expanded 'Unit 71: Power Generation' plus a separate 'Unit 72: Emergency power generation' - auxiliary house-power units dating to the original 2008 regas terminal, expanded for the liquefaction addition - but neither source discloses a generating-MW figure for Unit 71, and Unit 72 reads as standby/emergency, which is excluded from captive. MECHANICAL-DRIVE DETAIL: ECA LNG Phase 1's single APCI C3MR liquefaction train is refrigerant-compressor-driven, not electric: DOE FE docket 18-144-LNG (which incorporates ASEA's environmental-authorization letter ASEA/UGI/DGGPI/0233/2017 as an exhibit) identifies dedicated gas turbines driving both refrigerant compressor trains by equipment tag - the MR refrigerant High/Medium-pressure compressor turbine (G1-3101) and the propane refrigerant compressor turbine (G1-3102) - fed by the plant's own high-pressure fuel-gas system. No manufacturer/model disclosed in sources reviewed. Air Products' 2021 technology-award release separately confirms the train uses 'fuel-efficient mechanical drivers' alongside its coil-wound heat exchangers, consistent with shaft (non-electric) drive.

source_tier: EPC supply contract text (third-party contract aggregator) + 2 independent project sources
source_notes: Firebird LNG LLC (Phoenix Development Holding + MAD Energy JV; onshore liquefaction plant, ~4 mtpa design, anchor tenant of the planned Nickerie deepwater port/SEZ) executed a July 2022 EPC supply contract with Siemens Energy AB for an SCC6-800 6x1 combined-cycle power island - six gas-turbine generators, six HRSGs and one steam-turbine generator, rated 430 MW - explicitly to power 'its LNG facilities and port facilities.' Genuine electric generation, not shaft/mechanical drive. Independent trade press corroborates a 'gas-fired combined cycle power plant' as part of the phased development described in the developers' 2023 NIMOS environmental scoping submission. ELECTRIC CAPACITY: 430. ORCHESTRATOR NOTE: YELLOW: the 430 MW figure appears in only ONE source (the Siemens Energy SCC6-800 EPC supply contract text hosted by a third-party contract aggregator); neither corroborating URL carries the number. The captive verdict is robust regardless - a 6x1 combined-cycle power island is far above the >50 MW threshold - but treat 430 MW itself as single-sourced.

source_tier: operator's own fleet page + OEM press release + operator technical paper
source_notes: Atlantic LNG's four trains use the Phillips Optimized Cascade Process with GE Frame 5-series gas turbines in mechanical-drive configuration (shaft power directly turning the propane/ethylene/methane refrigeration compressors, zero MWe) - confirmed by a joint ConocoPhillips/Bechtel technical paper (LNG14, Doha, March 2004) giving per-train turbine counts and models, and independently corroborated by a GE Oil & Gas release on the Train 1 Frame 5/2C-to-5/2D compressor upgrade. The same paper also documents a SEPARATE dedicated on-site power-generation system: Solar Mars 100 gas-turbine generator sets (at least 4 added for the Train 4 expansion - one tied to the existing grid, three new - plus a pre-existing fleet serving Trains 1-3) feeding the complex's own 12.47 kV internal grid. Genuine electric captive generation therefore exists in addition to the mechanical-drive compressor turbines, though no source found discloses the aggregate nameplate MW of that generating fleet. MECHANICAL-DRIVE DETAIL: Train 1: 6x GE Frame 5C gas turbines mechanically driving the propane/ethylene/methane refrigeration compressors (2 per circuit); upgraded 2003-04 to Frame 5/2D spec, raising output 13% to 43,700 hp (~32.6 MW shaft) per unit (~196 MW aggregate shaft for Train 1 alone). Trains 2 & 3: 6x Frame 5D each, 2 per refrigeration circuit. Train 4: 8x Frame 5D turbine/compressor sets (3 propane + 3 ethylene + 2 methane) per the Phillips Optimized Cascade 'Two-Trains-in-One' design; aero-derivative alternatives (Rolls-Royce Coberra, LM-2500+/LM-6000) were evaluated for Train 4 and rejected in favour of more Frame 5D units. All four trains use gas-turbine MECHANICAL DRIVE for liquefaction refrigeration. The operator describes the resulting fleet as ~28 GE Frame 5-class turbine-compressors, the largest such fleet in the world - reported as BACKGROUND only, not a cited value, because that page failed the verifier (see verification_log). ORCHESTRATOR NOTE: Train 1 is mothballed and Train 5 cancelled; CaptiveGasPower is project-level so the value is staged to every unit-row. See qa_review for the separate Train-1 permanent-decommissioning / restructuring finding, which belongs to a follow-on Update batch.

source_tier: primary/regulatory (Nova Scotia EA registration + independent NS EA Review Panel report)
source_notes: Pieridae's 2013 Nova Scotia Environmental Assessment registration for Goldboro LNG explicitly lists a '180 MW Power Plant' as a dedicated project component, described as 'On-site (gas turbine) power generation to support the LNG facility and support services,' supplied by 'industrial gas turbines driven generator sets in an open cycle configuration' (Frame 6 turbines, N+1 sparing) feeding the facility's electric-motor-driven feed gas compressors and other site loads. The independent NS Environmental Assessment Review Panel's 2014 report separately confirms the project comprises 'a LNG facility... an electrical power generation plant... a 180 megawatt gas fired power plant.' MECHANICAL-DRIVE DETAIL: Design also included a fully SEPARATE set of mechanical-drive gas turbines: the two liquefaction trains' refrigerant compressors were to use gas turbine drivers (Frame 7) of approximately 160 MW shaft power per train (4 machines total for 2 trains, i.e. ~640 MW combined shaft power). These are NOT part of the 180 MW figure and do not generate electricity, so they are excluded from electric_mw. The 180 MW GOGPT entry corresponds only to the separate Frame-6-turbine electric generator plant, so the captive designation here rests on straightforward electricity generation, not on mechanical drive. ELECTRIC CAPACITY: 180.

source_tier: primary/regulatory (FERC certificate CP13-113) + Maryland DNR fact sheet + OEM
source_notes: Liquefaction main refrigerant compressors are mechanically driven by two GE Frame 7EA gas turbines (FERC Certificate CP13-113; GE project announcement). Waste heat from those turbines feeds HRSGs driving two 65 MW steam turbine generators = a 130 MW on-site bottoming plant built solely to meet the liquefaction facility's electric loads. Maryland PPRP: total on-site nameplate 210.9 MW (incl. legacy import-terminal units) used exclusively on-site, no export to grid. FERC: the steam turbines 'would not produce electricity for sale'. No PJM grid draw found for the liquefaction load. MECHANICAL-DRIVE DETAIL: Two GE Frame 7EA gas turbines directly drive (mechanical/shaft coupling) the two main LNG refrigerant-compressor trains, ~86 MW ISO shaft power each (~172 MW combined shaft). Separate from and additional to the 130 MW electric figure. ELECTRIC CAPACITY: 130.

source_tier: primary/regulatory (BC EAO Project Overview + GHG Technical Data Report) + national press
source_notes: BC EAO Project Overview + the project's GHG Technical Data Report (both joint-review filings) describe a phased power design. Permanently the project connects to the BC Hydro grid (electric-motor compressor drives). If that interconnection is delayed, the approved design falls back to purpose-built 'temporary floating power barges' - 8 gas turbine generator sets in combined cycle with steam turbines, net power 603 MW - supplying the same electric-motor compressors for up to 5 years post-startup, then decommissioned and removed. The project's own emissions accounting treats the barge scenario as a real operating case. MECHANICAL-DRIVE DETAIL: None - the FLNGs' main refrigerant compressor drives are electric motors in every scenario (grid-fed and barge-fed); no mechanical-drive gas turbines anywhere in the design. ELECTRIC CAPACITY: 603. ORCHESTRATOR NOTE: REVIEWER CALL - please decide before pasting. The COMMITTED design is grid electric-drive via BC Hydro; the 603 MW of purpose-built on-site gas generation is an APPROVED CONTINGENCY that builds only if the interconnection is delayed. The SOP's partially-captive and as-designed rules both point toward True, and the evidence is primary/regulatory and unambiguous about the facts - but whether an approved-but-conditional design element should set CaptiveGasPower is a definitional judgment, not a research gap. Staged yellow so it surfaces for that decision rather than being silently omitted.

source_tier: OEM press release (GE, equipment order) + OEM turbine brochure + trade press
source_notes: The two FLNG vessels actually committed to this project are Golar's Hilli Episeyo (first phase, 2.45 mtpa, arriving/operations 2027) and a second unit built on Golar's Fuji LNG hull under the 'MK II' project name (3.5 mtpa, 2028) -- NOT 'Gimi', which is a separate Golar FLNG chartered to BP for the Greater Tortue Ahmeyim project off Mauritania/Senegal; Golar's own fleet page lists Gimi and Fuji LNG as distinct vessels. Both committed vessels are self-contained, moored FLNG units with no shore-grid tie. Hilli Episeyo's own onboard power/drive configuration (originally built for its 2018-2026 Cameroon deployment and carried over to Argentina, since the Seatrium upgrade contract covers only mooring/life-extension/winterization, not a re-power) combines mechanical gas-turbine-driven refrigerant compression (GE PGT25+G4/2BCL, 4 trains) with steam-turbine-generator electric power (2 x 33 MW Peter Brotherhood units via waste-heat recovery) -- both onboard, both captive to the vessel/terminal, no external grid. MECHANICAL-DRIVE DETAIL: Hilli Episeyo's 4 liquefaction trains (Black & Veatch PRICO single-mixed-refrigerant) are each driven by a GE PGT25+G4 aeroderivative gas turbine directly mechanically coupled to a GE 2BCL centrifugal refrigerant compressor - shaft drive, no generator in this loop - per GE's own press release announcing the equipment order for the conversion (4 compression trains with PGT25+G4 drivers) and GE's PGT25 brochure (~34 MW class per unit), i.e. roughly 136 MW of shaft power across 4 trains, far above the >50 MW threshold. NO PUBLICLY SOURCED ELECTRIC GENERATION FIGURE EXISTS for this vessel, so electric_mw is deliberately left blank (see orchestrator note). MK II (Fuji LNG hull) will also license PRICO but its equipment order for Argentina is not yet publicly disclosed. ORCHESTRATOR NOTE: electric_mw deliberately BLANK. The researcher's '66 MW (2 x 33 MW Peter Brotherhood steam-turbine generators)' was removed at the QC gate: no cited source contains it, and it traces to a Wayback article about the GIMI conversion quoting a 26-MW turbine - the wrong vessel and the wrong number. The captive YES rests on the well-sourced mechanical side (4 x GE PGT25+G4 driving GE 2BCL compressors, ~136 MW shaft, off-grid moored FLNG).
